title: Warehouse Management and Operational Standards
summary: This thread covers the operational and legal framework for bonded warehouses and storage facilities. It maintains a consistent legal basis for rent, access, and liability, while introducing modern security protocols like electronic seals.

evolution.security: Integration of digital tracking and electronic sealing into traditional warehouse management.
evolution.procedure: Formalization of internal handover and custody protocols for warehouse staff.

timeline.change: Introduced specific internal security and handover protocols for warehouse officers.
Introduced modern technological definitions (e-seals/GPS) for facility security.

member_objects.clause_title: পদস্থ গুদাম কর্মকর্তার গুদামের দায়িত্ব গ্রহণ ও হস্তান্তর পদ্ধতি
member_objects.resolved_text:
২৮ । পদস্থ গুদাম কর্মকর্তার গুদামের দায়িত্ব গ্রহণ ও হস্তান্তর পদ্ধতি:

(১) মূল্যবান ও ট্রানজিট গোডাউনের পণ্য সংরক্ষণ/হস্তান্তর প্রক্রিয়া অনধিক ১৫ কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে সমাপ্ত করতে হবে।

(২) পদস্থ নতুন গুদাম কর্মকর্তা গুদামের নিরাপত্তা ব্যবস্থা যাচাইপূর্বক সঠিক রয়েছে কিনা নিশ্চিত করবেন।

(৩) পদস্থ গুদাম কর্মকর্তা দায়িত্ব প্রদানকারী/গ্রহণকারী কর্মকর্তার নিকট রেজিস্টার বর্ণনা এবং প্রদর্শনপূর্বক হস্তান্তর করবেন।

(৪) বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংকে স্থায়ীভাবে/অস্থায়ীভাবে স্বর্ণবার/স্বর্ণালংকার, রৌপ্য/রৌপ্যবার এবং মুদ্রার জমাদানের বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংকে কপি রেজিস্টার লিপিবদ্ধ অনুযায়ী প্রমাণক যাচাই সাপেক্ষে দায়িত্ব প্রদানকারী কর্মকর্তা দায়িত্ব গ্রহণকারী কর্মকর্তার নিকট হস্তান্তর করবেন।

(৫) লিকার ও cigarette বাংলাদেশ পর্যটন কর্পোরেশনকে প্রদানের মাসিকভিত্তিক হিসাবের প্রমাণক নিশ্চিত হয়ে দায়িত্ব বুঝে নিবেন।

(৬) নিলামযোগ্য পণ্য বা নিলামকৃত পণ্যের তথ্যাদি রেজিস্টার লিপিবদ্ধের প্রমাণক নিশ্চিত হয়ে দায়িত্ব গ্রহণকারীর কর্মকর্তা দায়িত্ব বুঝে নিবেন।

(৭) ধ্বংসযোগ্য পণ্যের বিবরণ, তালিকা এবং বর্তমান অবস্থান তথ্যাদি রেজিস্টার লিপিবদ্ধের প্রমাণক নিশ্চিত হয়ে দায়িত্ব গ্রহণকারীর কর্মকর্তা দায়িত্ব বুঝে নিবেন।

(৮) গোডাউনের আওতাধীন সকল ধরণের লকার ও অন্যান্য প্রয়োজনীয় কক্ষের তালা এবং চাবি সচল অবস্থায় বুঝে নিবেন। গোডাউনের প্রধান গেট এর তালা ও চাবি নতুন কর্মকর্তার পদায়ন ভিত্তিক পরিবর্তন করে হস্তান্তর করতে হবে।

(৯) সমস্ত মালামাল বুঝিয়ে দেয়ার সময় প্রতিটি রেজিস্টারে লিপিবদ্ধ অনুযায়ী মালামালের সংখ্যা, পরিমাণ উল্লেখ করে গ্রহণকারী ও প্রদানকারী কর্মকর্তা নিয়ন্ত্রণকারী ও তত্ত্বাবধানকারী কর্মকর্তার উপস্থিতিতে নোট তৈরি করবেন। নোটের প্রত্যেক পৃষ্ঠায় গ্রহণকারী ও প্রদানকারী কর্মকর্তাদের সীল সহ স্বাক্ষর থাকবে।

Warehouse Operations: The handover of warehouse responsibilities for valuable goods and transit cargo must be completed within a maximum of fifteen working days.
The incoming warehouse officer is responsible for verifying the security status of the facility as part of the formal handover process.

Operational procedures require the outgoing and incoming officers to verify all goods against official registers and prepare a joint note in the presence of supervisory staff, with all pages signed and sealed by both parties.
Customs Warehouse: The outgoing officer must hand over the keys and locks of all lockers and rooms to the incoming officer while ensuring they are in working condition.
The master keys and locks for the main warehouse gate must be changed upon the appointment of a new officer during the handover process.
Precious Metals and Currency: The transfer of gold, silver, and currency items deposited with the Bangladesh Bank requires the verification of proof documents against the register before the responsibility is formally handed over.
Bangladesh Parjatan Corporation: Incoming warehouse officers must verify the monthly records and proof of delivery for liquor and cigarettes handed over to the Bangladesh Parjatan Corporation.
Auctionable Goods: Responsibility for auctionable or auctioned goods is transferred only after the incoming officer verifies the relevant register entries and supporting evidence.
Perishable Goods: The transfer of perishable goods requires the incoming officer to confirm the accuracy of the item descriptions, lists, and current physical locations against the official register records.

Customs Act 1969: The term Act is defined as the Customs Act 1969, and any terms not explicitly defined in these rules shall carry the same meaning as attributed to them under this Act.
Electronic Seal: An electronic seal is a device used to secure goods in containers or transport vehicles, incorporating GPS technology for location tracking and tamper-evident features to prevent unauthorized manipulation of the seal or the contents.
National Board of Revenue: The term Board is defined as the National Board of Revenue, which was established under the National Board of Revenue Order 1972.
Rapid Response Team: A Rapid Response Team refers to the specific unit formed and tasked under the provisions of Rule 13 of these regulations.
Lock: A lock is a security mechanism used on containers, vehicles, or rail wagons that integrates with an electronic seal and allows for remote monitoring and operation via a central monitoring center.
Customs Service: This service encompasses the application and maintenance of electronic seals and locks on transport vehicles or containers, the verification of seal integrity, and the authorized opening of these devices in the presence of customs officials.
Service Recipient: A service recipient includes parties such as importers, exporters, transit and transshipment clients, customs agents, and logistics or transport service providers who utilize the customs sealing and locking services.
Service Provider: A service provider is any entity formally appointed under the provisions of Rule 3 to deliver specific customs-related security and sealing services.
Central Monitoring Center: The central monitoring center is the facility established under the mandate of Rule 14 to provide oversight and manage the electronic monitoring of seals and locks.
Customs Alert System: An alert is an automated notification system transmitted via email, web-based platforms, or mobile messaging to report events such as seal activation, tampering, loss of signal, unauthorized route deviation, or unexpected delays during transit.

৯৬। ভাড়া এবং ওয়্যারহাউস-পাওনা পরিশোধ।— (১) কোন ওয়্যারহাউসকৃত পণ্যের মালিক আপাততঃ বলবৎ কোন আইনের অধীন নির্ধারিত হারে অথবা যে ক্ষেত্রে এইরূপ ভাড়া নির্ধারিত নাই সেই ক্ষেত্রে কমিশনার অব কাস্টমস (বন্ড) কর্তৃক অথবা অন্য কোন কমিশনার অব কাস্টমস কর্তৃক নির্ধারিতহারে অথবা ওয়্যারহাউস মালিক এবং ওয়্যারহাউসকৃত পণ্যের মালিকের মধ্যে চুক্তি দ্বারা নির্ধারিত হারে ভাড়া এবং অন্যান্য চার্জ ওয়্যারহাউস রক্ষককে পরিশোধ করিবেন।
(২) উপধারা (১) এর অধীন নির্ধারিত ভাড়া এবং অন্যান্য চার্জ সম্বলিত হারের একটি তালিকা দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ করে এমন অংশ উক্ত ওয়্যারহাউসে প্রদর্শন করিতে হইবে।
(৩) যদি কোন ভাড়া অথবা অন্যান্য চার্জ উহা প্রদেয় হওয়ার তারিখ হইতে দশ দিবসের মধ্যে পরিশোধ করা না হয়, তাহা হইলে ওয়্যারহাউসকৃত পণ্যের মালিককে যথাযথ নোটিশ প্রদানের পর এবং যথাযথ কর্মকর্তার অনুমতিক্রমে ওয়্যারহাউস রক্ষক অপরিশোধিত ভাড়া এবং অন্যান্য চার্জ আদায়ের জন্য যেরূপ যথেষ্ট হয় পণ্যের সেইরূপ অংশ (ওয়্যারহাউসকৃত পণ্যের কোন স্থানান্তর সত্ত্বেও) বিক্রয়ের ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করিতে পারিবেন।

Bonded Warehouse Operation: The owner of bonded goods is responsible for paying rent and associated charges to the warehouse keeper according to rates set by law, custom authorities, or mutual agreement.
Warehouse keepers are required to display a list of these rates in a prominent location within the facility for public access.

In the event that rent or other charges remain unpaid beyond the specified grace period, the warehouse keeper may, after providing notice and receiving approval from customs officials, sell a portion of the stored goods to recover the outstanding dues.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs is authorized to determine the rates for rent and charges applicable to bonded warehouse goods in cases where such rates are not otherwise provided by law.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer of customs must provide their authorization before a warehouse keeper can proceed with the sale of bonded goods for the recovery of unpaid rent or charges.

member_objects.resolved_text: 84. Application to warehouse.- When any dutiable goods have been entered for warehousing and assessed under section 80, the owner of such goods may apply for leave to deposit the same in any warehouse appointed or licensed under this Act.

Goods: Once dutiable goods have been entered for warehousing and duly assessed, the owner may request authorization to deposit them in an approved or licensed warehouse.
Warehouse: The law provides a framework for the deposit of assessed dutiable goods into any facility that has been officially appointed or licensed to act as a warehouse.
Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the legal authority for the appointment or licensing of warehouses where owners of assessed goods may apply to store their inventory.
Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner of goods that have been assessed for warehousing is authorized to apply for permission to store those items in a licensed or appointed warehouse.

member_objects.clause_title: Warrant to be given when goods are warehoused
member_objects.resolved_text:
90. Warrant to be given when goods are warehoused.- (1) Whenever any goods are lodged in a public warehouse or a licensed private warehouse, the warehouse-keeper shall deliver a warrant signed by him as such to the person lodging the goods.
(2) Such warrant shall be in such form as the Board may from time to time prescribed, and shall be transferable by the endorsement; and the endorsee shall be entitled to receive the goods specified in such warrant on the same terms as those on which the person who originally lodged the goods would have been entitled to receive the same.
(3) The Board may, by notification in the official Gazette, exempt any class of goods from the operation of this section.

Public Warehouse: The warehouse-keeper must provide a signed warrant to the person lodging goods when they are stored in a public warehouse.
Private Warehouse: When goods are lodged in a licensed private warehouse, the warehouse-keeper is required to issue a signed warrant to the depositor.
Warehouse Keeper: The warehouse-keeper is responsible for issuing a signed warrant to any person lodging goods in their facility.
Warehouse Warrant: A warehouse warrant serves as a transferable document when endorsed, allowing the holder to receive the specified goods under the same conditions as the original depositor.
The form of the warehouse warrant must comply with requirements prescribed by the National Board of Revenue.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to prescribe the required form for warehouse warrants.
The Board is empowered to exempt specific classes of goods from the warrant requirements of this section through an official Gazette notification.
Goods: The National Board of Revenue may exempt certain classes of goods from the requirements governing warehouse warrants.

member_objects.clause_title: Access of owners to warehoused goods
member_objects.resolved_text:
93. Access of owners to warehoused goods.- (1) Any owner of goods lodged in a warehouse shall, at any time within the hours of business, have access to his goods in the presence of an officer of customs, and an officer of customs shall, upon application for the purpose being made in writing to the appropriate officer, be deputed to accompany such owner.
(2) When an officer of customs is specially employed to accompany such owner, a sum sufficient to meet the expense thereby incurred shall, subject to rules, be paid by such owner to the appropriate officer, and such sum shall, if the appropriate officer so directs, be paid in advance.

Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner of goods stored in a warehouse is entitled to access their goods during business hours.
The owner must request access in writing and may be required to pay the expenses incurred for a customs officer to accompany them, potentially in advance.
Warehouse: This is the facility where goods are lodged and where the owner is granted the right to access their items under official supervision.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer receives the written application from the owner to access warehoused goods and is responsible for deputing a customs officer to accompany the owner.
This officer is empowered to direct the payment of expenses for the customs officer's attendance and may require such payment to be made in advance.
Customs Officer: An officer of customs must be present to accompany the owner of the goods whenever they access their warehoused items.
The officer's attendance for such purposes is subject to rules regarding the recovery of expenses incurred.

member_objects.clause_title: Payment of rent and warehouse dues
member_objects.resolved_text:
96. Payment of rent and warehouse dues.- (1) The owner of any warehoused goods shall pay to the warehouse-keeper rent and other charges at the rates fixed under any law for the time being in force or where no rates are so fixed, at such rates as may be fixed by the Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs or by agreement between the owner of the warehouse and the owner of warehoused goods.
(2) A table of the rates of rent and other charges fixed under sub- section (1) shall be displayed in a conspicuous part of such warehouse.
(3) If any rent or other charges are not paid within ten days from the date when they become due, the warehouse-keeper may, after due notice to the owner of the warehoused goods and with the permission of the appropriate officer, cause to be sold (any transfer of the warehoused goods notwithstanding) such portion of the goods as may be sufficient to realise the unpaid rent and other charges.

Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner is legally obligated to pay rent and other warehouse charges to the warehouse keeper at rates determined by law, by official designation, or by mutual agreement.
The owner is subject to the sale of their goods by the warehouse keeper if rent and charges remain unpaid after the prescribed notice period and with appropriate customs permission.
Warehouse Keeper: The warehouse keeper is entitled to collect rent and charges from the owner of warehoused goods at rates established by law or designated authorities.
The warehouse keeper is required to display a table of fixed rent and charge rates in a prominent location within the warehouse.

The warehouse keeper is empowered to sell a sufficient portion of the stored goods to recover unpaid rent and charges, provided that notice is given and the permission of the appropriate officer is obtained.
Commissioner of Customs: This authority is empowered to fix the rates for rent and warehouse charges in instances where no other rates have been established by law.
Warehouse: The facility must display a visible table outlining the fixed rates of rent and other charges applicable to the storage of goods.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer must provide the necessary permission before a warehouse keeper can sell stored goods to recover unpaid rent and charges.
Warehoused Goods: These goods are subject to rental and operational charges while stored in a warehouse.
A portion of these goods may be sold by the warehouse keeper to settle outstanding financial dues if payment is not made within the specified time frame following formal notice.

Warehouse Keeper: table of fixed rent and charge rates

member_objects.clause_title: Allowance in case of volatile goods
member_objects.resolved_text: 110. Allowance in case of volatile goods.- When any warehoused goods of such class or description as the Board having regard to the volatility of such goods and the manner of their storage may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify are, at the time of delivery from a warehouse, found to be deficient in quantity and the 2[Commissioner] of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board] is satisfied that such deficiency is on account of natural loss, no duty shall be charged on such deficiency.

Warehoused Goods: The law allows for a deficiency in the quantity of certain volatile warehoused goods at the time of delivery from the warehouse.
No customs duty is chargeable on such deficiency if the relevant customs authority is satisfied that the loss was caused by natural factors during storage.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to specify by notification in the official Gazette which classes of goods qualify as volatile for the purpose of granting duty allowances on natural storage losses.
The Board also has the authority to authorize specific Commissioners of Customs to verify and approve such natural loss claims.
Commissioner of Customs: This official is authorized to review and satisfy themselves that a deficiency in warehoused goods is attributable to natural loss, thereby exempting the goods from customs duty on that missing portion.
Any Commissioner of Customs authorized by the Board may determine if a deficiency in volatile warehoused goods is due to natural causes, allowing for an exemption from duty on the lost quantity.
Warehouse: The provision applies to goods stored in a warehouse, specifically regarding the condition of the goods at the time they are delivered from the facility.

Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer of customs must provide their authorization before a warehouse keeper can proceed with the sale of bonded goods for the recovery of unpaid rent or charges.

Goods: Once dutiable goods have been entered for warehousing and duly assessed, the owner may request authorization to deposit them in an approved or licensed warehouse.
Warehouse: The law provides a framework for the deposit of assessed dutiable goods into any facility that has been officially appointed or licensed to act as a warehouse.
Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the legal authority for the appointment or licensing of warehouses where owners of assessed goods may apply to store their inventory.
Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner of goods that have been assessed for warehousing is authorized to apply for permission to store those items in a licensed or appointed warehouse.

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Warrant to be given when goods are warehoused
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
90. Warrant to be given when goods are warehoused.- (1) Whenever any goods are lodged in a public warehouse or a licensed private warehouse, the warehouse-keeper shall deliver a warrant signed by him as such to the person lodging the goods.
(2) Such warrant shall be in such form as the Board may from time to time prescribed, and shall be transferable by the endorsement; and the endorsee shall be entitled to receive the goods specified in such warrant on the same terms as those on which the person who originally lodged the goods would have been entitled to receive the same.
(3) The Board may, by notification in the official Gazette, exempt any class of goods from the operation of this section.

Public Warehouse: The warehouse-keeper must provide a signed warrant to the person lodging goods when they are stored in a public warehouse.
Private Warehouse: When goods are lodged in a licensed private warehouse, the warehouse-keeper is required to issue a signed warrant to the depositor.
Warehouse Keeper: The warehouse-keeper is responsible for issuing a signed warrant to any person lodging goods in their facility.
Warehouse Warrant: A warehouse warrant serves as a transferable document when endorsed, allowing the holder to receive the specified goods under the same conditions as the original depositor.
The form of the warehouse warrant must comply with requirements prescribed by the National Board of Revenue.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to prescribe the required form for warehouse warrants.
The Board is empowered to exempt specific classes of goods from the warrant requirements of this section through an official Gazette notification.
Goods: The National Board of Revenue may exempt certain classes of goods from the requirements governing warehouse warrants.

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Access of owners to warehoused goods
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
93. Access of owners to warehoused goods.- (1) Any owner of goods lodged in a warehouse shall, at any time within the hours of business, have access to his goods in the presence of an officer of customs, and an officer of customs shall, upon application for the purpose being made in writing to the appropriate officer, be deputed to accompany such owner.
(2) When an officer of customs is specially employed to accompany such owner, a sum sufficient to meet the expense thereby incurred shall, subject to rules, be paid by such owner to the appropriate officer, and such sum shall, if the appropriate officer so directs, be paid in advance.

Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner of goods stored in a warehouse is entitled to access their goods during business hours.
The owner must request access in writing and may be required to pay the expenses incurred for a customs officer to accompany them, potentially in advance.
Warehouse: This is the facility where goods are lodged and where the owner is granted the right to access their items under official supervision.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer receives the written application from the owner to access warehoused goods and is responsible for deputing a customs officer to accompany the owner.
This officer is empowered to direct the payment of expenses for the customs officer's attendance and may require such payment to be made in advance.
Customs Officer: An officer of customs must be present to accompany the owner of the goods whenever they access their warehoused items.
The officer's attendance for such purposes is subject to rules regarding the recovery of expenses incurred.

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Payment of rent and warehouse dues
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
96. Payment of rent and warehouse dues.- (1) The owner of any warehoused goods shall pay to the warehouse-keeper rent and other charges at the rates fixed under any law for the time being in force or where no rates are so fixed, at such rates as may be fixed by the Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs or by agreement between the owner of the warehouse and the owner of warehoused goods.
(2) A table of the rates of rent and other charges fixed under sub- section (1) shall be displayed in a conspicuous part of such warehouse.
(3) If any rent or other charges are not paid within ten days from the date when they become due, the warehouse-keeper may, after due notice to the owner of the warehoused goods and with the permission of the appropriate officer, cause to be sold (any transfer of the warehoused goods notwithstanding) such portion of the goods as may be sufficient to realise the unpaid rent and other charges.

Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner is legally obligated to pay rent and other warehouse charges to the warehouse keeper at rates determined by law, by official designation, or by mutual agreement.
The owner is subject to the sale of their goods by the warehouse keeper if rent and charges remain unpaid after the prescribed notice period and with appropriate customs permission.
Warehouse Keeper: The warehouse keeper is entitled to collect rent and charges from the owner of warehoused goods at rates established by law or designated authorities.
The warehouse keeper is required to display a table of fixed rent and charge rates in a prominent location within the warehouse.

The warehouse keeper is empowered to sell a sufficient portion of the stored goods to recover unpaid rent and charges, provided that notice is given and the permission of the appropriate officer is obtained.
Commissioner of Customs: This authority is empowered to fix the rates for rent and warehouse charges in instances where no other rates have been established by law.
Warehouse: The facility must display a visible table outlining the fixed rates of rent and other charges applicable to the storage of goods.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer must provide the necessary permission before a warehouse keeper can sell stored goods to recover unpaid rent and charges.
Warehoused Goods: These goods are subject to rental and operational charges while stored in a warehouse.
A portion of these goods may be sold by the warehouse keeper to settle outstanding financial dues if payment is not made within the specified time frame following formal notice.

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Allowance in case of volatile goods
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text: 110. Allowance in case of volatile goods.- When any warehoused goods of such class or description as the Board having regard to the volatility of such goods and the manner of their storage may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify are, at the time of delivery from a warehouse, found to be deficient in quantity and the 2[Commissioner] of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board] is satisfied that such deficiency is on account of natural loss, no duty shall be charged on such deficiency.

Warehoused Goods: The law allows for a deficiency in the quantity of certain volatile warehoused goods at the time of delivery from the warehouse.
No customs duty is chargeable on such deficiency if the relevant customs authority is satisfied that the loss was caused by natural factors during storage.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to specify by notification in the official Gazette which classes of goods qualify as volatile for the purpose of granting duty allowances on natural storage losses.
The Board also has the authority to authorize specific Commissioners of Customs to verify and approve such natural loss claims.
Commissioner of Customs: This official is authorized to review and satisfy themselves that a deficiency in warehoused goods is attributable to natural loss, thereby exempting the goods from customs duty on that missing portion.
Any Commissioner of Customs authorized by the Board may determine if a deficiency in volatile warehoused goods is due to natural causes, allowing for an exemption from duty on the lost quantity.
Warehouse: The provision applies to goods stored in a warehouse, specifically regarding the condition of the goods at the time they are delivered from the facility.
